job.style: a rule explained with two contrasting examples

passage: To understand 3D shapes, we must distinguish between their visible features and their actual properties. A polyhedron is a solid made of flat polygonal faces. For any convex polyhedron, Euler’s formula states that the number of faces (F) plus the number of vertices (V) minus the number of edges (E) always equals two, written as F + V - E = 2. Consider a cube: it has 6 faces, 8 vertices, and 12 edges. Applying the formula, 6 + 8 - 12 equals 2, which confirms the rule. In contrast, consider a cylinder. A cylinder is not a polyhedron because it has a curved surface. While it has two circular flat faces, it also possesses two curved edges where the flat surfaces meet the curved side. If you look at a cylinder from the top, you see a circle, but from the side, you see a rectangle. These different views are necessary to understand the full shape, as no single view reveals the entire object. Furthermore, a pyramid is named specifically by the shape of its base. A square pyramid has a square base and four triangular side faces, totaling five faces, not four. Understanding these rules helps us identify solids correctly by their geometric properties rather than just their appearance.

items.evidence: For any convex polyhedron, Euler’s formula states that the number of faces (F) plus the number of vertices (V) minus the number of edges (E) always equals two, written as F + V - E = 2.
items.q: A convex polyhedron has 5 faces and 6 vertices. How many edges must it have?
options: 9 edges
11 edges
13 edges
7 edges
items.explain: By Euler's formula, 5 + 6 - E = 2, so E must be 9.

wrong.why: uses only faces plus 2 and forgets vertices

items.evidence: A cylinder is not a polyhedron because it has a curved surface.
items.q: Why is a cylinder not counted as a polyhedron?
options: It has a side that is not flat
It has no edges because it is round
It has circles instead of square faces
It has three faces, which is too few
items.explain: A polyhedron has only flat faces, but a cylinder has a curved side.

wrong.why: thinks round solids have no edges
thinks polyhedron faces must be squares
counts the curved surface as a face

items.evidence: While it has two circular flat faces, it also possesses two curved edges where the flat surfaces meet the curved side.
items.q: Meena says a cylinder has no edges since it is round. What is actually true?
options: It has two curved edges at its rims
It has no edges, being completely round
It has two straight edges down its side
It has one edge around its middle
items.explain: A cylinder has two curved edges where its flat circles meet the curved side.

wrong.why: thinks a round solid has no edges
thinks edges must be straight lines
guesses an edge where none is described
